titulo: Articles, plural and c'è / ci sono: Gender and singular articles

aula.titulo: Articles, plural and c'è / ci sono
aula.objetivo: Use the definite and indefinite articles with the right gender, form plurals by changing the vowel, and say what exists with «c'è» and «ci sono». Avoid the English-speaker traps: one «the» for every noun, plurals with «-s», and false friends such as «camera».

itens.pt: the room, the bedroom (not a camera!)

blocos.titulo: Every noun has a gender, and «the» has four faces
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: English has one «the» for everything: «the book», «the pen», «the window». Italian has a different «the» depending on the gender of the noun (masculine or feminine) and on the first sound of the word. STEP 2: masculine singular: «il» before most consonants («il libro»), «lo» before «s» + consonant, «z», «gn» and «ps» («lo studente», «lo zaino»), and «l'» before a vowel («l'amico»). STEP 3: feminine singular: «la» before a consonant («la penna», «la finestra») and «l'» before a vowel («l'amica»). STEP 4: «l'» is the same for both genders, so the noun itself and the ending show which one it is: «l'amico» (male friend), «l'amica» (female friend). STEP 5: gender is a property of the word, not of the meaning. A book is not «male» in any real sense. Most nouns ending in «-o» are masculine and most nouns ending in «-a» are feminine: «il libro», «la penna». STEP 6: nouns ending in «-e» can be either: you must learn them with their article («il nome», «la notte»). STEP 7: learn each new noun with its article from the very start: not «libro» but «il libro». STEP 8: the indefinite articles follow the same logic: «un libro», «uno zaino», «una penna», «un'amica». «Uno» is used where «lo» is used.
blocos.comparacao: English has no grammatical gender, so this is the first place where you cannot reuse your instincts. Do not try to guess the gender from the meaning: learn the article together with the word and let the ending help. Another English habit to drop: the article must be repeated in Italian lists («il libro, la penna e lo zaino»), but English lets you say «the book, pen and backpack».

tabela.singolare: il libro · lo zaino · lo studente · l'amico
la penna · la finestra · la camera · l'amica

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: some Italian words look like English words and mean something else. «La camera» is a room, usually a bedroom: the device is «la macchina fotografica». STEP 2: «il libro» is a book, not a library: a library is «la biblioteca» and a bookshop is «la libreria». STEP 3: «la penna» is a pen. A pencil is «la matita». STEP 4: «lo studente» is a student of any age, school or university. STEP 5: «l'amico» is a friend. Keep a notebook of false friends, with the article, and add each new one when you meet it.
blocos.comparacao: «Camera» and «libreria» are two classic English-speaker mistakes. A «library» is not «la libreria»; it is «la biblioteca». And «la camera» is a room, not what you take photos with.

tabela.forma: camera → room; libreria → bookshop; biblioteca → library

erros.motivo: «Libreria» is a shop that sells books; to borrow one, go to the «biblioteca».

itens.explicacao: Before «s» + consonant the masculine article is «lo».
«Libro» is masculine and starts with a simple consonant.
Before a vowel, the article is shortened.

blocos.enunciado: Look around the room and name five objects with the right article, in Italian.
Say the four faces of «the» aloud: «il», «lo», «la», «l'». Which sounds trigger «lo»?
